newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to up despite mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to higher Thursday in moderate activity, with prices correcting after recent weakness though little upside was seen as long as mild weather in the East persists, sources said.
"We may have overreacted to the downside, but I don't see it screaming up. There's not much demand and it would only take one or two cargoes to upset the balance," said a trader. In

New York Harbor, physical one percent climbed 40 cents to the high-$17 a barrel area on news of a 100,000-barrel sale for Feb 3-7 delivery, 50 percent fixed at $18 and 50 percent at a formula low minus 25 cents, traders said.

NYH February one percent paper sold at $18.10, up 40 cents or more on the day, with buyers and sellers still seen around that number. March paper was quoted at $17.75-18.00, with Q2 pegged at $17.40-70, traders said.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour edged up a quarter to $18.75-19.00 after reports late Wednesday of a 100,000-barrel deal for Feb 1-10 delivery at $19.
High sulphurs in New York were talked unchanged.
While relatively mild East Coast weather should slow demand, traders said some high sulphur material moving out of the U.S. Gulf to the Caribbean will help trim bloated stocks.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent firmed slightly to the $16.25 area, while three percent held steady in the high-$14s.
Milder weather in New York pressured city gate gas prices down another five to 10 cents to about the $3.30/mmBtu level. NYH one percent resid climbed to a $2.84/mmBtu equivalent.
